Open the short listening checklist
  • Width: use a stereo track; move Width, compare, and check for unintended jumps or strange stereo behavior.
  • Loud: use your normal material; check the more aggressive setting for objectionable distortion or loss of musical movement.
  • Volume Match off: compare Mastered playback with the saved master at the same player volume. Note any unexplained level or tone difference.
  • Album: listen through transitions in the saved continuous album and a few numbered tracks. Check order and intended consistency.
  • Real hardware stress: with the engineer, use the existing high-rate/long files while playing, changing settings and switching Original/Mastered. Note clicks, silence, freezes or device-recovery trouble.

Reply format: “Width: pass. Loud: issue at 1:24 on [track], [setting]. VM-off: pass. Album: pass. Stress: [result].”

What I fixed

Five improvements are implemented locally. Preset sound and mastering behavior stay as intended.

  • Export controls now fit the app. WAV/MP3 and bitrate selectors use the dark studio styling and clearer labels.
  • The track title has a YES Master signature. The brand mark and cleaner title treatment connect the hero area to the rest of the interface. A native rendering issue found during the recheck was corrected too.
  • Meters stay inside their panel. On short desktop windows, the Peak reading could spill into the export area. The layout now keeps the full meter stack visible.
  • Album retry shows the current job. Cancelling and retrying no longer leaves the old “export cancelled” message beside fresh progress.
  • Album exports have a “Show files” button. You can go directly to the saved output. If the file manager cannot open, the path remains available.

Independent audio results

The Standard WAV and Advanced MP3 both measured −14.0 LUFS. Each retained the expected 3:26.72 duration. The two-track continuous MP3 measured 6:08.72, matching the combined source lengths. Album track numbering matched the final order.

True-peak and loudness-range readings matched the app's receipts within the measurement tool's displayed rounding. Earlier exports remained unchanged.

The engineering plan

These tasks belong to engineering. Your job is to supply the decisions and listening results above.

  1. Finish the MP3 distribution package. Include the pinned dependency notices, required source/relinking materials and reproducible instructions in the actual release. A successful local MP3 export is only part of this.
  2. Build the approved replacement candidate. Run fresh checks on the exact version; produce complete Mac and Windows downloads, updater signatures and checksums.
  3. Prove install and update journeys. Test the actual downloads, first run, save/export recovery and update success/failure/retry. Include startup window fit and monitor changes: the computer-use session showed initial cropping that cleared after Zoom, but its changing display size may be involved. Reproduce that before deciding whether an app fix is needed. Record the file identity so results cannot accidentally refer to an older build.
  4. Support the narrow listening session. Prepare the corrected build and existing files, then investigate only failed or still-unresolved checks.
  5. Activate the download only after approval. Verify the real destination and beta date. Keep optional signup disabled unless a provider and consent details are chosen.
Optimization opportunities — measured first

MP3 export is the first profiling target. One observed Track MP3 export took about 14.5 seconds; most of that was in encoding and delivered-file verification. The comparable WAV observation was about 2 seconds, but settings and background workload differed, so this is not a clean benchmark.

  • Separate encoder and verification timings on ordinary, high-rate and long files.
  • Investigate whether a duplicated pre-encode measurement can be removed while keeping delivered results exact.
  • Profile frequent playback-driven UI updates before restructuring them.
  • Consider a small cap for cached setting variants if long-session measurements justify it.

No speculative speedup or sound change was introduced. Existing shared-audio memory and bounded background workers were retained.

Items that do not need to expand this launch

Linux/mobile expansion, new preset voicing, Adaptive Compressor activation, founder-offer promises, a custom domain, newsletter integration and paid signing do not need to be bundled into this audit's fixes. Preserve the already approved free-beta route and handle optional items deliberately.
